data.body:
Progress. The fix is committed locally (Change-Id I1d214d73df17cafc33bc346ebc3da28403bd0a98) and `make verify` is running.

Pre-merge Windows evidence comes from the throwaway branch `w1-diag-opcert-acl`, which runs the 28 tests plus the new test file on windows-latest.
- Run 44590213544 (fix applied): op-cert signing now composes and signs on Windows. 34 passed, 1 skipped (the POSIX-only test), 3 failed. All 6 new tests pass, including the real-ACL test `test_windows_copy_acl_names_only_the_current_user`.
- The 3 failures are separate defects. The ACL fix exposed them, because compose_signer used to fail first:
  - `test_completion_pass_spawn_ceiling` and `test_completion_fail_spawn_ceiling` fail because `project_ensures._PROJECTS_REL_PATH` uses `os.path.join` inside a git revision path (`tickets:.bridge_state\projects.json`). The lookup misses on Windows, so the seed rewrites projects.json on every sweep, which adds spawns. Filed as undamaging-ashamed-wasp. With that one-line fix applied, run 44591481319 shows both passing.
  - `test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` fails because its nested run's TMPDIR and basetemp sit under a deep tmp_path, and git hits "Filename too long" (MAX_PATH). Filed as flowered-nonvalued-mink (test-only fix). Run 44592408164 is testing it.

Ordering: wasp and mink land on main BEFORE this change, so that deleting `openssh-key-acl.args` here does not turn the main sweep red. AC2 is checked on main after all 3 land.

Portability: the new code runs only where os.name == "nt". It uses subprocess with an argument list, a timeout and lenient decoding, and adds no POSIX-only API.
